### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is SAGE's publisher-wide AI policy (no journal-specific ISP addendum found). Assistive AI (grammar/language/structural editing) needs no disclosure. Generative AI whose output affects methodology, analysis, results, or conclusions must be disclosed at submission for editorial evaluation. AI tools cannot be credited as an author. Undisclosed GenAI use is grounds for rejection; fabricating data, AI-conducted interviews, and AI-generated images presented as original data are explicitly prohibited. Policy text found is the generic SAGE corporate policy page, not a page naming International Journal of Social Psychiatry specifically, so confidence that it applies unmodified to this journal is moderate, not confirmed first-hand. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Allowed under standard SAGE preprint policy: authors must enter the preprint DOI at submission and notify the editorial office; manuscript must not be updated on the preprint server while under peer review; preprint citations should be updated to the published version once available.

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** General social-psychiatry empirical/epidemiological research and reviews on the role of social, cultural, and environmental factors in psychiatric disorders; mental health of international/displaced/minority communities (war refugees, LGBTQ+, indigenous peoples); service development and evaluation papers; cross-disciplinary work bridging psychiatry with sociology/anthropology.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Empirical/epidemiological studies, Systematic and narrative reviews, Cross-cultural / cross-national comparative studies, Service evaluation research, Qualitative studies from anthropology/sociology perspectives
